title: Prefetch safety-net: per-request microprobe + fallback scheduler for arch/seq-len kernel picking
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Kernel selection currently relies on offline profiling and coarse seqlen buckets. For mixed workloads we observe p99 latency regressions when rare long-prefill requests hit a kernel optimized for short-prefill throughput. Goal: Implement a lightweight per-request microprobe + prefetch safety-net that (1) quickly detects the best kernel candidate for the current request given model, architecture, and effective sequence-length, (2) caches a confidence-weighted mapping keyed by (model-version, arch-family, seqlen-bucket), and (3) provides an immediate fallback scheduler when observed latency or KV-cache pressure deviates from expectations. Non-goals: This ticket does not change operator-level autoscaling or pricing logic; it focuses on per-request kernel routing and a runtime-level fallback mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce microprobe probe path that runs O(1) tiny kernel microbench on first N requests per model-arch pair
Confidence cache correctly stores and expires entries; TTL and decay parameters configurable via flags
Rollback/fallback triggers: if real-time token latency exceeds predicted by >30% for two consecutive requests, scheduler switches kernel and emits trace events
No increase in median latency >5% for stable workloads; p99 reduced by at least 10% on mixed-length traces in internal benchmark suite
Unit, integration, and e2e tests validated; feature flag gated and canaryed to <5% traffic during rollout
metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency delta (canary vs baseline)
fraction of requests that used microprobe vs cache hit
confidence cache hit rate and TTL churn
implementation_steps: Design microprobe harness: lightweight kernel invocation path with strict timeout (e.g., 1–2ms budget)
Add per-request feature vector (model-version, arch-family, effective-seqlen, KV-cache-state) to probing API
Implement confidence cache: sharded LRU with decay and per-key confidence score; expose flags for TTL and min-samples
Implement fallback scheduler: rule engine that subscribes to traces/latency signals and atomically swaps kernel route for request streams
Instrumentation: add trace spans, metrics and dashboards; emit events for probe result, cache update, and fallback activation
Safety and limits: probe budget global throttle, per-model probe-sample ceiling, and opt-out via model config
Write unit tests for probe timeout and cache behavior; integration tests using mixed-prefill traces; load tests to validate overhead
Create feature flag, rollout plan, and revert path in infra
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal traffic only (perf team + devs) — validate correctness and metrics (2 weeks)
Canary: 1% customer traffic on runtime-1.20 with feature flag enabled; monitor p99 and fallback rate (1 week)
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with 24h observation windows and automatic rollback on safety thresholds
Full launch after 2 weeks stable at 20% and no regressions at p99/p50/p95
risks: Probe overhead could increase median latency if not strictly budgeted; mitigation: global probe budget and off-path async probes where possible
False positives in fallback triggering could cause oscillation between kernels; mitigation: hysteresis and backoff windows
Confidence cache staleness when hardware topology changes (new GPU drivers/firmware); mitigation: invalidate cache on node/driver upgrades
Edge-case models with pathological attention patterns may need model-specific tuning; mitigation: model opt-out and recording of failing sequences for offline analysis
open_questions: What is the optimal microprobe budget that balances signal vs overhead? Start with 1ms and iterate based on perf traces?
Should probes be synchronous on the critical path for cold sessions, or kicked off async and used on subsequent requests?
How to encode effective-seqlen: prefill length, decode length estimate, or a combined metric?
Integration with existing kernel advisor: do we continue to write to the same kernel catalog or maintain a separate runtime cache?
